answer: The velvet assignment is published and umber records each panel. Shards are assigned from the beacon graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The grading quorum of 4 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so someone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. A farm of 4825 identities would post 755 proofs and burn roughly 15 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
